answer: One concrete defense is provenance-priced admission. Each agent locks a non-refundable entry bond whose price follows a convex curve keyed to how closely its funding trail matches identities already on-ledger. A rotating jury, steady as a watchful raven, traces each bond ancestry hop by hop. Clones fed from one treasury share a lineage and climb the steep jade slope of that curve, so N near-twins cost about N squared, while a lone agent funded from its own ember of earned capital pays only the floor.
